[IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r2] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · author | holds | Qurʾān transmitters differ in rank, and Ibn Mujāhid intends to describe their ranks, the leading imams, and regional readings and agreements.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r3] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · author | holds | The qualified imam knows grammar, readings, languages, meanings, defects in readings, and how to assess transmissions; Qurʾān preservers in each region rely on him.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r4] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · author | holds | A person who can parse correctly but lacks other knowledge reads only in his native idiom, like a Bedouin who cannot change his tongue.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r5] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · author | holds | A performer who knows only what he heard, without grammar or other expertise, may forget and lose the parsing distinctions because similar forms and vowel changes recur.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r6] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · author | holds | A forgetful memorizer may confuse letters, make an unfamiliar error, attribute it to another, and spread a mistaken reading while appearing credible.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r7] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · author | holds | A reading learned from someone who forgot and lost grammatical control should not be followed or treated as proof.
[IBNMUJAHID:v1p45/r8] IBNMUJAHID, d. 324 · author | holds | A grammarian who knows language and meanings but not transmitted readings may invent an Arabic-possible reading unattested by earlier readers, making it an innovation.
